notes: Crowd ratings are rounded aggregates observed across major review platforms. Pillar scores (0-10) are editorial judgments applied uniformly by the rubric in METHODOLOGY.md.

restaurants.name: Windy City Pie
restaurants.signature: The caramelized cheese crown — a molten parmesan ring fused to the pan wall
restaurants.blurb: Started as a clandestine SoDo parking-lot handoff: call ahead, text on arrival, trade cash for a deep pan pie. Now a proper Phinney Ridge dining room where your pizza is walked to the table like a bottle of Barolo. The bake is engineered — a buttery biscuit-crumb base, a tomato layer with real acid, and a cheese wall that shatters.

restaurants.name: Delancey
restaurants.signature: Long-fermented Washington wheat dough, blistered and pliant
restaurants.blurb: The pie that recalibrated Seattle's expectations in 2009 and still sets the floor for everyone else. Brandon Pettit's dough ferments for days on local wheat, then goes into a wood oven that leaves leopard char without sacrificing the fold. The crocodile-hide underside is the whole argument.

restaurants.name: Cornelly
restaurants.signature: Seasonal produce treated as the main event, not a garnish
restaurants.blurb: The Delancey brain trust pointed at the farmers market. Pizza is the backbone but the kitchen behaves like a full restaurant — charred brassicas, whipped ricotta, whatever the week gave them. It is the most convincing case in the city that a pizzeria can also be a serious vegetable restaurant.

restaurants.name: Moto Pizza
restaurants.signature: A 72-hour dough baked into a crisp-edged slab with absurd topping architecture
restaurants.blurb: The hardest reservation in Seattle pizza and it isn't close — drops sell out in minutes and the waitlist has become part of the folklore. What arrives justifies more of the hype than it has any right to: a tall, airy, crunchy-bottomed pan pie built with real precision.

restaurants.name: Serious Pie
restaurants.style: Blistered thin crust, applewood stone oven
restaurants.signature: Sweet fennel sausage and roasted peppers on a charred, cracker-edged base
restaurants.blurb: Tom Douglas's applewood-fired room has been packing communal tables since 2006 and remains the most reliable pizza in the core. The crust runs thin and aggressively blistered; the topping list stays short and Pacific Northwest-literate. Still the default answer when someone visiting asks.

restaurants.name: Dino's Tomato Pie
restaurants.signature: Sauce-on-top square slices under a red neon glow
restaurants.blurb: A love letter to New Jersey pizza parlors, right down to the bar-forward room and the sauce ladled over the cheese. The squares are thin, crackly and built for a beer at 11pm. Nothing else in Seattle is doing this style with this much conviction.

restaurants.name: Lupo
restaurants.signature: Sourdough base with a menu that turns over with the market
restaurants.blurb: A small, tightly-run room where the dough is naturally leavened and the toppings change on the kitchen's whim. The bake sits in the sweet spot between Neapolitan softness and a crust with actual structure — you can pick up a slice without it surrendering.

restaurants.name: The Independent Pizzeria
restaurants.signature: A tiny wood oven and a menu that refuses to grow
restaurants.blurb: Barely bigger than a living room, a few blocks from Lake Washington. The wood oven runs hot, the pies come out fast and thin, and the whole operation is an argument for doing one thing at a scale you can actually control. Long a critics' quiet favorite.

restaurants.name: Tutta Bella
restaurants.signature: Verace Pizza Napoletana certification — 90 seconds at 900°F
restaurants.blurb: Washington's first VPN-certified pizzeria and the reason a generation of Seattleites knows what a true Neapolitan pie is supposed to taste like. It is textbook by design: soppressata piccante, San Marzano, fior di latte, a soft and soupy center. Consistent across every location, which is its own achievement.

restaurants.name: Pagliacci Pizza
restaurants.signature: The Primo Gusto slice, available approximately everywhere, forever
restaurants.blurb: The civic baseline. Since 1979 Pagliacci has been the pizza Seattle actually eats — a reliable slice on a corner in nearly every neighborhood, seasonal specials that are better than they need to be, and a delivery operation that borders on infrastructure. Not the city's best pie. Comfortably its most important.
